key_insight: A finite-volume convolution unit lets CNNs operate directly on non-uniform, non-orthogonal meshes, enabling turbulence super-resolution beyond structured grids.
engineering_relevance: This makes data-driven flow reconstruction usable on the meshes actually employed in wall-bounded and complex-geometry CFD simulations.
method: Replace standard convolution with finite-volume convolution operators built from axis-wise gradient, averaging, and identity terms.
Use an exact 3D convolution decomposition into successive 1D-axis operations that remain well-defined on arbitrary polyhedral cells.
Condition the network on a Van Driest damping input to encode wall proximity and near-wall physics.
evidence_signal: The model was tested on 4× downsampled channel-flow and pipe-flow cases and reproduced instantaneous velocities, Reynolds stresses, anisotropy, and spectra beyond the low-resolution Nyquist limit, with transfer to an unseen elliptic pipe.
watch_item: Generalization to new geometries is promising but small-scale energy was modestly overpredicted on the unseen elliptic pipe, so mesh/geometry transfer should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Extending convolutional neural networks to finite-volume meshes for fine-scale reconstruction of wall-bounded turbulence
